entry_thesis: Oracle is down ~50% from its September 2025 all-time high of $326.90, trading near $155 on fears that its $300B OpenAI deal represents reckless cash burn on an unprofitable customer — but the consensus is wrong. The company just pre-announced a $553B remaining performance obligation backlog (up 325% YoY), 44% cloud revenue growth, and 84% OCI infrastructure growth for the quarter ending Feb 28, all of which the market has failed to price. At ~18x forward earnings for a business growing total revenue 22%+ organically, ORCL is the cheapest large-cap cloud infrastructure name in the market. Fiscal Q3 earnings on March 10 are 4 days away and represent the catalytic moment where the market's AI-bubble-fear narrative collides with the actual numbers.
risk: If Oracle's Q3 earnings disappoint or management lowers guidance, the stock could leg down further given the technical damage already done; the bull case requires the market to reward a company spending aggressively on AI capex in an environment where investors are punishing AI spenders.
catalyst: Fiscal Q3 2026 earnings release on March 10 — consensus expects $1.70 non-GAAP EPS and ~$16.9B revenue; a beat with strong OCI growth and RPO expansion will force a re-rating; multiple Buy-rated analysts (Jefferies PT $320, TD Cowen PT $250) provide fundamental floor and will upgrade targets post-print.
